label: heart-s4
summary: The model is mostly linear on the log-odds scale. Its direct terms carry the ranking: training AUC is 0.9424 with them and 0.6906 when they are replaced by their mean. Vessel count is the strongest driver: the typical patient is at 16% predicted risk with no vessels coloured and above 99% with three. On top sit three small nonlinear parts. A gate opens for the 15 training patients with a fixed thallium defect and changes their log-odds by -2.42 on average, so the typical patient with a fixed defect is placed at 2% against 16% with a normal scan and 37% with a reversible defect; it is a correction fitted to a small group whose outcome rate is 60%, rather than evidence that a fixed defect is protective. A heart-rate unit steepens the downward slope of risk with maximum heart rate once it switches on, between 130 beats per minute and 140 beats per minute for the typical patient. An atypical-angina hinge changes the log-odds of the 42 patients it acts on by -0.113. Worth checking: high fasting blood sugar lowers predicted risk through its direct edge (typical patient with a normal scan: 16% to 4%), although the training outcome rates of patients with and without high fasting sugar are close (45% and 44%).

resisted: No part was moved to resisted. The atypical-angina hinge is described rather than explained: it is a fixed offset for one chest-pain level and switching it off moves training AUC from 0.9424 to 0.9422. The fixed-defect gate is explained as a correction but is fitted to 15 rows, and the ST-T abnormality input of the heart-rate unit acts on 2 rows, too few to read as a finding.
